1) Exact wording/scope: confirm the precise language (does it expressly name “lost profits” and “consequential/indirect/special” damages, is it mutual, and does it employ unambiguous “in no event” phrasing) — if explicit and broad, courts are far more likely to bar lost‑profit claims; if ambiguous or narrowly worded, a court may construe exceptions for consequential losses.
